belief: If something is hard, it can’t be God’s will.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that if something is hard it can’t be God’s will, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Teaching that God’s will always feels peaceful and easy. Using “closed doors” as the only sign of God’s leading. Wanting to avoid pain or conflict. Discouragement when following God led into difficulty. A culture that values comfort.
teaches: God’s will often includes hard things. The apostles taught that we must endure many hardships to enter the kingdom of God. Jesus prayed in Gethsemane, “Not My will, but Yours be done,” and God’s will led Him to the cross. Scripture says suffering produces perseverance, character, and hope. Ease is not proof of God’s will, and difficulty is not proof that you are outside it. We fix our eyes on Jesus, who endured the cross for the joy set before Him.
self_statements: If it’s this hard, God must not be in it.
Difficulty means I took a wrong turn.
I should quit because it’s hard.
A closed door always means no.
If I were in God’s will, everything would go smoothly.
errors: Deciding God’s will by how easy or hard something feels.
Treating every difficulty as a sign from God.
Using “it’s hard” as a reason to quit what God has called you to.
Overlooking how often God’s people faced hardship in His will.
questions: Was the cross easy for Jesus? Was it God’s will?
What did the apostles say about hardships?
What does suffering produce, according to Romans 5:3–4?
Is ease always a sign of God’s will?
Am I quitting because God is leading me away or because it is hard?
What wise counsel do I need about this situation?
How can I fix my eyes on Jesus in this difficulty?
truth: Something being hard does not mean it isn’t God’s will. God’s will led Jesus to the cross, and His people often face hardships. Suffering can produce perseverance, character, and hope. I can seek wisdom about my situation and, when God is calling me to stay, fix my eyes on Jesus and endure.
hw_questions: Was the cross easy? Was it God’s will?
What did the apostles say about hardships?
Is ease always a sign of God’s will?
Am I quitting because of God or because it’s hard?
How can I fix my eyes on Jesus?
hw_truths: Hard things can be part of God’s will.
Jesus prayed, “Not My will, but Yours be done.”
Suffering can produce perseverance, character, and hope.
I can fix my eyes on Jesus and endure.
Difficulty is not proof that I am outside God’s will.
I am hard pressed but not crushed.
log: Each day, write one hard thing I faced and one way God helped me endure it.
name_example: Sarah can rejoice in her sufferings, because she knows that suffering produces perseverance; perseverance, character; and character, hope.
actions: and write how Jesus prayed in His hardest moment.
Write down a hard situation you are in,
and ask: “Is God calling me to leave, or to endure?” Seek counsel.
List people in Scripture who did God’s will through hardship,
such as Joseph, Daniel, and Paul.
in the hard thing God has given you this week.
tracker: One way God helped me endure
prayer: Father, thank You that Jesus was willing to do Your will even when it was hard. Help me reject the lie that if something is hard, it can’t be Your will. Give me wisdom to know when to stay and strength to endure, with my eyes fixed on Jesus. Not my will, but Yours be done. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
